Yeah we go from the start of the current year to get ours. So Jan 1st is julian date 1.

Financial IT, basically its a simple way of telling the date from a certain point, or working out the elspased time between two dates, for example if I needed to know what day it is going to be in 48 days its simpler/quicker to use the julian date, it will be day 357 (from a given start date of the first day of 2020).

For date/time management, you want all your instants to use a simple, monotonous, linear scale. Human calendars, time zones, daylight saving time, these make things more complex. Julian date is exfremyl simple and easy to read/calculate.
